method: One launcher run of the whole roster on the final artifact; each non-passing suite then run alone on a pre-repair export (base) and, where the first comparison did not settle it, again on a final-tree export (rerun). Receipts are the SHA-256 of each suite's log block plus its failure evidence lines; full logs were kept outside the repository.
baseSha: 49b5f39a (pre-repair HEAD; exported to a throwaway repository and built)
finalSha: 389d4169 (published HEAD) plus the uncommitted closeout edits that the roster ran on
rerunSha: throwaway export of the final working tree (commit 24228e17, tree identical to the working tree after the roster, built)
limits: Evidence lines are extracted from log text. A suite is 'matched baseline' when every failure line of the final run also appears (after masking numbers, ids, ports and database names) in the pre-repair run of the same suite. A final run that fails for an additional reason that prints no recognizable failure line would not be detected by this comparison.
The launcher counts the four explicit opt-in suites as child failures; they are listed as 'explicit opt-in', not as passed or failed.
Full logs are not committed (they hold database names and ports). Each record carries the SHA-256 of its log block and the failure lines.
Two suites (c1 browser, the d-v contact-actor browser) are not clean pass/fail signals on any tree: see their notes.
